## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #222 at **992fd0a1b55e95843550dc5fc6d3475e4bac4611**, under C33/C34. Reviewed the five-file delta and directly relevant registration, lease and session-event paths. No unauthorized admission or normal-use registration wedge established.

The early brake returns the existing `NativeHolderCurrent` refusal, not a seat or capability (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:500-514`). It retains HTTP 409 and `{retryable:true,hold:"native-holder"}`; no pane, session or grant field is added to the existing predecessor-based diagnostic (`http/mod.rs:1239-1245`).

Explicit foreign-session conflicts still precede it. Passing the brake still requires host/pane proof and locked roster/spawn checks (`registration.rs:477-492,516-525,754-1018,1560-1698`). Absent/tombstoned/non-native predecessors, different process identities, expired leases and outranking pass through rather than being admitted by the brake. Lease matching uses the existing incarnation and boot-grace rules without process observation (`delivery/mod.rs:515-547`).

The extension checks joined-session identity and SDK event provenance. New primary prompts or live resume events rearm it; replayed history does not. Counter reset, generation wakeups, losing-timer cleanup and success reset remain explicit (`.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs:163-179`; `store.mjs:109-132,185-223,263-270`). The ten-minute check remains a recovery path when no event arrives. Takeover may require that check or a qualifying event; promptness is not a continuous liveness-monitor guarantee.

**S222-N001, accepted C33 qualification:** holder status is now disclosed before host proof, so strict information/refusal-stage equivalence is not claimed. Registration remains authenticated and excluded from peer-key routes (`http/mod.rs:436-446,751-790`); the disclosure stays inside the trusted local-key account boundary. **C33: same-user, out of scope** as a per-seat information-isolation block.

**S222-N002, proof/correctness qualification:** the early refusal can mask a later hard host/pane/spawn refusal as a retryable hold, and its snapshot is outside the registration lock. It does not establish atomic equivalence during concurrent holder removal. No unauthorized access or persistent normal-use wedge was established; retry/event recovery remains.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | None established in scoped changes under C33 | - |

The daemon regression at `registration.rs:3666-3696` asserts zero observer calls on the early-refusal path; extension tests cover threshold, rearm, success reset and live-versus-history resume (`store.test.mjs:5795-5860`). Zero process reads is scoped to an existing-holder refusal, not a real takeover that reaches host proof. Live cost/after-deploy measurements remain the performance verdict's scope.

**CI proof:** clean detached worktree HEAD and GitHub/remote heads agree; GitHub reports CLEAN and all five checks successful. Run [42763950727](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42763950727) checked merge `e42c53eef0eee0d1aea64e31fdea204d70987394`, with parents main `765e3320bb524701ddc3bce9db7c5c11bf060165` and this exact head. Rust reports **2,413 passed, 6 skipped**; successful JUnit artifact `13738418647` includes existing lease-expiry/takeover witnesses. Node 22 logs explicitly show both F162 stop/rearm regressions passing and native tests **349 passed, zero failed**.

Static source review and existing CI only. No local builds/tests, real process/pane probes, config/credential reads or product mutations.
